comments.text:
My mom and I bought three necklaces for Christmas gifts. The man said- let me wrap them. He took them to the back. At Christmas we saw he had exchanged them for smaller stones. 
Another example: my mom bought a gold necklace as a gift. It broke and I took it back to have it repaired. The jeweler said  I cant fix this junk. I then said that my mom bought it there. The guy tried to bluster his way out but he couldn’t. 
Beware. Jewelers trick elderly customers without blinking an eye! It’s awful! My mom was literally tricked by two well known jewelers.

replies.text: @Bigredmoon007 Sometimes...I retired, I have a traditional pension and I collect Social Security...I have a 2016 Toyota Rav 4 with only 8,000 miles on it...I also have a 2023 Toyota Corolla, I paid cash for both...I now have no car payment, and these should last me the remainder of my life, Never another car payment again...Remember this, Yes Buying a new car you lose thousands, BUT what if you never have to buy another car again...On the other hand...Leasing, you will have a car payment forever...and by the time your lease is up the car is 5 years older or more...and you still owe thousands unless you do the same thing all over again...Lease a new car and keep making payments for ever...Leasing is IMHO a rip off....If you can afford to buy a car, buy it and take care of it....
